result.summary: Our patch fixes CVE-2018-12542 at exactly the same place and with the same mechanism as the vendor fix: URL-decode `context.normalisedPath()` first, null-check the decoded value, normalize the alternate Windows path separator `\` to `/`, and only then run `Utils.removeDots(...)` so that RFC-3986 dot-segment removal actually sees `\..\` sequences before the string is concatenated onto the webroot and handed to the FileSystem sink. The only divergence is that the official fix gates the replacement on `File.separatorChar != '/'` while ours applies `replace('\\','/')` unconditionally — security-wise a strict superset (identical on Windows, stricter on Unix), but it deliberately discards the platform guard the maintainers added to preserve backslash-as-a-legal-filename-character on Unix, and our added test `testEscapeWindows` hard-codes that divergent Unix behavior. Execution evidence is essentially absent: the POV never reproduced pre-patch (this is a Windows-only traversal, and the harness ran on a `/`-separator platform) and zero regression tests were executed, so the verdict rests on code reasoning rather than observed behavior.
result.root_cause: `StaticHandlerImpl.handle` fed the URL-decoded request path to `Utils.removeDots`, which only recognizes `/` as a segment separator, so a percent-encoded backslash (`%5c..%5c`) survived dot-segment removal as a literal `\..\` and was concatenated onto the webroot, where a `\`-separator filesystem (Windows) reinterpreted it as traversal above the base directory.

dimensions.rationale: Both Windows path separators are collapsed to '/' before dot-segment removal, so the whole `%5c..%5c`/`\..\` traversal class — not just the observed payload — is neutralized before the path reaches getFile/FileSystem; double-encoding (`%255c`) is not re-decoded so it stays an inert literal.
dimensions.evidence: StaticHandlerImpl.handle: `String path = Utils.removeDots(uriDecodedPath.replace('\\', '/'));` replacing `Utils.removeDots(Utils.urlDecode(context.normalisedPath(), false))`; sink at StaticHandlerImpl.java:611-614 (getFile → webRoot + Utils.pathOffset(path)) now receives a dot-free, single-separator path.
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Fixes the flaw itself — the separator/normalization mismatch at the URL→filesystem trust boundary — at the single choke point every downstream consumer (sendStatic, sendDirectory, getFile) inherits, not at a caller or in an error path.
dimensions.evidence: Change is inside StaticHandlerImpl.handle (official method_start 132–152), the same location the reference fix chose; ordering decode → separator-normalize → removeDots matches official exactly.
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: Covers both separator characters on all platforms and all sibling paths, since `path` is normalized once in handle before any branch (index page, directory listing, sendStatic); no additional tainted entry point to the sink exists beyond what the official fix covers.
dimensions.evidence: Taint trace endpoints Utils.java:373/387 (pathOffset) and StaticHandlerImpl.java:186/192/264/266 all consume the single `path` local produced at the patched line; official fix touches only the same method.
dimensions.label: Completeness / variants

dimensions.rationale: Same defensive strategy, same file/method, same statement ordering as the reference; differs only by omitting the `File.separatorChar != '/'` guard, which makes it a strict security superset rather than a contradiction.
dimensions.evidence: Ours: decode → null-check → `replace('\\','/')` → removeDots. Official: decode → null-check → `if (File.separatorChar != '/') path = path.replace(File.separatorChar, '/')` → `path = Utils.removeDots(path)`.
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: No execution evidence at all (0 regression tests ran, POV never reproduced pre-patch), and the unconditional replace plausibly over-restricts on Unix, where '\' is a legal filename character the official fix deliberately preserved — `/foo\bar` now resolves to `webroot/foo/bar` instead of the literal file.
dimensions.evidence: Execution results: regressions_ran=0, regressions_passed=null, pov_before_reproduced=false; patch line `uriDecodedPath.replace('\\', '/')` lacks the official's `if (File.separatorChar != '/')` guard; added test `testEscapeWindows` asserts 200 for `/%5c..%5cindex.html` on any platform, locking in the divergence.
dimensions.label: Functional correctness

dimensions.rationale: No new weakness introduced — `String.replace(char,char)` is a constant-time literal substitution (no ReDoS), the null-check is now correctly performed before removeDots, and every behavior change is in the more-restrictive direction; only a minor edge risk of remapping Unix backslash filenames to a different (still in-webroot) file.
dimensions.evidence: `String uriDecodedPath = Utils.urlDecode(...); if (uriDecodedPath == null) {...return;} String path = Utils.removeDots(uriDecodedPath.replace('\\','/'));` — null handled before use; resulting path still passes through removeDots, so no escape above webRoot.
dimensions.label: No new defects

dimensions.rationale: Six changed lines confined to the vulnerable method plus one focused test; no unrelated edits or refactors.
dimensions.evidence: Single hunk at StaticHandlerImpl.java:135-149; only other change is `testEscapeWindows` in StaticHandlerTest.java.
dimensions.label: Minimality

dimensions.rationale: Uses genuine canonicalization (normalize every separator to one form, then RFC-3986 dot-segment removal) applied before the path is used, not a blocklist of '../' — the CWE-022 defense-of-record as the vendor implements it — but neither ours nor the official adds the belt-and-braces step of resolving the real absolute path and verifying containment inside webRoot (so e.g. symlinks under webRoot remain unchecked).
dimensions.evidence: `Utils.removeDots(uriDecodedPath.replace('\\','/'))` performs normalization, not string blocklisting; no `toRealPath()`/`startsWith(webRoot)` containment check exists at getFile (StaticHandlerImpl.java:611-614), matching the official fix's scope.
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: The `\`→`/` replacement is unconditional, whereas the official fix guards it with `if (File.separatorChar != '/')`. On Unix/Linux a backslash is a legal filename character, so our patch makes files whose names contain '\' unreachable and silently remaps requests like `/foo\bar` to `webroot/foo/bar`. This is a security superset but a deliberate divergence from the maintainers' behavior-preserving choice; adding the platform guard would make the patch semantically equivalent at no security cost.

No execution evidence supports the fix or the absence of regressions: pov_before_reproduced=false (the Windows-only traversal cannot reproduce on the '/'-separator test host), pov_after_present=false, and regressions_ran=0 / regressions_passed=null. The verdict rests entirely on code reasoning; the StaticHandler suite should be run, ideally with a separator-parameterized test, before the no-regression claim can be trusted.

The added test `testEscapeWindows` asserts `/%5c..%5cindex.html` → 200 on every platform, which is only true because of the unconditional replace. Under the official (platform-guarded) fix that request 404s on Linux, so this test would fail if the patch were later aligned with upstream — it encodes the divergence as expected behavior rather than testing the Windows-specific fix.

Neither our patch nor the reference adds a post-resolution containment check (canonicalize the concatenated path with toRealPath() and verify it stays under webRoot). Normalization-only defenses leave adjacent traversal vectors — e.g. symlinks inside the webroot pointing outside it — unaddressed. Out of scope for this CVE, but it is why mitigation_soundness is not a 5.
